name: consistent-naming
description: Enforce consistent naming conventions across the codebase for variables, functions, classes, and files
author: community
content:
## Consistent Naming Conventions

### Variables & Functions
- Use camelCase for variables and functions: `getUserName`, `isActive`
- Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants: `MAX_RETRIES`, `API_BASE_URL`
- Boolean variables start with is/has/can/should: `isLoading`, `hasError`
- Functions start with a verb: `fetchData`, `calculateTotal`, `handleClick`

### Classes & Types
- Use PascalCase: `UserService`, `HttpClient`, `ApiResponse`
- Interfaces don't use I prefix: `User` not `IUser`
- Enums use PascalCase with PascalCase values: `Color.DarkBlue`

### Files
- React components: PascalCase (`UserProfile.tsx`)
- Utilities/hooks: camelCase (`useAuth.ts`, `formatDate.ts`)
- Test files: match source (`UserProfile.test.tsx`)

### Avoid
- Single letter names (except loop counters `i`, `j`)
- Abbreviations unless universally understood (`btn` → `button`)
- Negative booleans: `isNotReady` → `isReady` (invert logic)
